ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening under Ley 23 de 2015, as amended, and UAF risk-based resolutions, applied to all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the United Kingdom OFSI sanctions list, Panama's domestic anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing databases, and commercial PEP databases; any person identified as a politically exposed person (PEP), including family members and close associates, must receive enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring; failure to comply is subject to administrative penalties and suspension of the entity's registration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Plataforma de Servicios en Línea (Oficina Virtual del Registro Público), accessible through https://www.registropublico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script and must be sufficiently distinguishable from existing names; names in non-Latin scripts are transliterated into Spanish phonetic equivalents using the Latin alphabet; Spanish-language words may not be replaced by foreign-language equivalents where a recognised Spanish term exists; all filings submitted to the Registro Público must be in Spanish or accompanied by a certified Spanish translation prepared by an authorised perito traductor.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation certificate is valid for 30 calendar days from issuance; if the incorporation deed is not registered within that window, the applicant may file a fresh reservation request with payment of the applicable search and reservation tariff. Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written reconsideration brief with the Dirección General del Registro Público within five business days of notification, attaching evidence of the phonetic search and distinctiveness of the proposed name; if the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may pursue an administrative appeal and ultimately a contentious-administrative action before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia. In parallel, the applicant may immediately reserve a distinct alternative name to avoid delay of the incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible at the pre-incorporation stage where the registered office is the address of the licensed Panamanian resident agent, which is sufficient for holding and administrative purposes. However, for the ISIC 3250 automated point-of-care IVD manufacturing scope, a virtual office alone is not sufficient: the entity must obtain a physical commercial establishment in Panama with a municipal operating permit and a sanitary registration from the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) before commencing manufacturing activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 55-65% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by MINSA or municipal authorities within the first 12 months after obtaining the sanitary manufacturing license; approximately 10-15% probability of inspection where the entity operates solely as a non-operating holding or administrative vehicle with no physical production facility.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (Sociedades Anónimas), as amended; applicable sections relating to incorporation, capital, registered office, resident agent, directors, and officers
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección Mercantil (Public Registry of Panama, Commercial Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución y Pacto Social (Public Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association) filed with the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed under Ley 32 de 1927; the corporation must state an authorized capital and issue at least one share. No escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation hereby issues and accepts subscription for its authorized capital shares, fully paid in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation; that the registered office be and is hereby established at [Registered Office Address, Panama]; that the Directors appointed in the incorporation charter continue in office; that [Name] be and is hereby elected President, [Name] Treasurer, and [Name] Secretary; that the Corporate Seal be adopted; that banking signatories and the resident agent remain designated as required by Law 32 of 1927; and that officers are authorized to execute all documents and pay all fees necessary to register, license, and lawfully commence manufacturing operations for the Corporation's IVD products.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Registration Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Dirección de Registro y Certificación, and online via Panamá Digital portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal name reservation request with the proposed Sociedad Anónima name. Obtain a certificate of non-conflicting name or reservation certificate. File the initial entry request with the Public Registry's commercial section and pay the corresponding reservation fee.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (usually ending in S.A.)
Notarized application letter or digital submission form
Copy of applicant's valid identification or power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or questioned, submit an alternative name or file an administrative reconsideration request with supporting clarity of distinction within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Panama City or any notary authorized in Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Pacto Social y Estatutos before a Panamanian notary. The deed must state the corporate name, object, registered office, authorized capital, board of directors, resident agent appointment, and initial share issuance. Notarize the deed and obtain certified copies for subsequent registry filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation and bylaws
Notarized initial membrete or corporate profile
Identity documents and evidence of resident agent acceptance
Certificate of name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial protocol corrections are required, amend the draft deed and re-notarize before the same notary; any deficiency in content must be cured by a notarial correction instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Public Deed of Incorporation with the Public Registry's Commercial Section. Pay the registry fee based on the authorized capital and obtain the company's registration certificate and corporate entry number (ficha).
required_dossiers: Original Public Deed of Incorporation plus notarized copies
Certificate of corporate name reservation
Fiscal receipt for registry fee payment
Form of registry data and authorization of the resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct the specific observations from the Public Registry, file an amended deed or clarifying brief, and pay any supplementary fee. Judicial or administrative review is available in case of wrongful refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Municipal Operating Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, and the Municipality of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Public Registry entry is complete, apply to the DGI for a tax identification number (RUC) and obtain the corporate tax registration certificate. Register for the aviso de operación with the relevant municipal authority and obtain the municipal operating permit or business license.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Public Deed of Incorporation
Copy of the resident agent appointment and passport or identification
Proof of registered office address
RUC application form and taxpayer profile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration or municipal notice is rejected, remedy the deficiency by updating the corporate address, submitting a corrected form, or providing the outstanding municipal clearance and paying the corresponding taxes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Records, Seal, and Bank Signatory Designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate officers and the resident agent, with verification by the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the company's statutory corporate records book, adopt the corporate seal, and execute the first board resolution establishing bank signatories and officer authorizations. Prepare share certificates and maintain minutes of the organizational meeting.
required_dossiers: Corporate records book (stock and register book)
Board resolution appointing officers and signatories
Share subscription and payment evidence
Corporate seal and specimen signature forms
Bank account opening instructions if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Public Registry or a bank queries signatory authority, pass a curative board resolution and file a certified copy with the registry or financial institution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección Nacional de Regulación de Productos y Establecimientos de Salud, together with Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Registro Industrial
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Sanitaria de Funcionamiento para Establecimiento Fabricante de Dispositivos Médicos y Diagnóstico In Vitro (Sanitary Operating License for Medical Device and IVD Manufacturing Establishment)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección Nacional de Evaluación y Control Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I – Informe de Impacto Ambiental (low to moderate risk) for IVD manufacturing activities with minimal hazardous waste; full Estudio de Impacto Ambiental (Categoría II/III) is required if biological waste, VOC emissions, or discharge volumes exceed statutory thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Panama's national effluent regulations (e.g., Decreto Ejecutivo No. 158 de 1998) requiring wastewater pH within 6-9, BOD5 not exceeding 100 mg/L, COD not exceeding 200 mg/L, and total suspended solids below 100 mg/L; VOC and fume emissions controlled under MINSA workplace air guidelines; all biohazardous and infectious waste must be inactivated and disposed through a certified hazardous waste handler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate by Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, structural load inspection and building occupancy clearance by the Municipality of Panama's engineering department, and occupational health and safety inspection certificate from Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) confirming compliance with workplace welfare, electrical safety, and machinery guarding requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama City; under Law 365 of 2023 the DGI and the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) are being integrated into the Autoridad Nacional de Ingresos Públicos (ANIP), with the DGI e-platform remaining the transitional filing gateway. Primary portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa ('Tu Agencia en Números' / TAN, SISCO e-services).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the S.A. before a Panamanian notary and register the public deed, resident agent (agente residente), and registered office with the Registro Público de Panamá. Step 2: File the Aviso de Operación with the respective Municipio and, for IVD manufacturing, obtain the sanitary license/operational permit from the Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas (DNFD-MINSA). Step 3: Submit the electronic RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) application via Portal DGI attaching the public deed, notarized corporate resolutions, passport copies of non-resident shareholders/directors, local lease/adress proof, bank account certificate from a Panamanian bank, and the municipal Aviso de Operación. Step 4: Receive the RUC certificate activated for ISR, ITBMS, and customs operations; procure the DGI-compliant digital signature (firma digital) for electronic invoicing. Step 5: If employing staff, register as employer with the Caja del Seguro Social (CSS). Minimum capital is not required by law; no share capital deposit evidence is demanded for non-resident ownership. Lead time: approximately 10-25 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation | Territorial_Scope: the S.A. is an independent legal and tax entity under Ley 32 de 1927 and the Código Fiscal. Corporate income tax (ISR) applies exclusively to net income derived from Panamanian-source activities; foreign-source dividends, interest, capital gains, and offshore service profits fall outside the ISR base. Pass-through treatment is not available to an S.A.; the entity itself files ISR, administers dividend withholding where applicable, and is the registered ITBMS taxpayer. Tax-exempt zone alternatives exist (Colón Free Zone, SEM multinational headquarters regime) but do not alter the default S.A. classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no U.S.-style check-the-box election and no general fiscal consolidation. Available statutory elections include: (i) the presumed-income election, whereby an authorized taxpayer may compute ISR on 4.67% of gross taxable revenue instead of fully documented net profits; (ii) dividend distribution elections affecting the applicable withholding treatment on distributions from taxed profits, managed in the corporate minutes; (iii) the SEM (Sede de Empresa Multinacional) election under Law 41 of 2007 for qualifying multinational headquarters, granting ITBMS incentives and tax-stability comfort for foreign-source service income; and (iv) the election to attribute controlled foreign-company income pursuant to the transparency rules of Law 254 of 2021, relevant for hybrid mismatches and CFC substance. Each S.A. files separately; no group-level election is permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS - Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios, a VAT-type tax governed by Título III of the Código Fiscal, Law 15 of 1995 as substantially amended by Law 76 of 2019, administered by the DGI/ANIP.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD/PAB 0.00 - no de-minimis threshold for corporations: every S.A. conducting commercial, industrial, or professional activities in Panama must obtain the RUC and register for ITBMS before issuing invoices or operating under the Aviso de Operación. The simplified fixed-quota ITBMS regime is reserved for individuals and micro-sole proprietorships with annual gross income up to approximately USD 36,000; a manufacturing S.A. is not eligible for that exemption and must register under the general ITBMS rules irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica) is mandatory for all ITBMS taxpayers under DGI Resolution 201-3274 (June 2022), with phased migration across taxpayer categories concluded by 2024. Invoices must be issued in structured XML through a DGI-authorized e-invoicing solution (in-house API or certified commercial provider), digitally signed with a Panama PKI certificate (firma digital), and transmitted to the DGI's centralized e-invoicing repository in near real time; batch transmission is permitted only for smaller taxpayers. Every accepted invoice receives a unique DGI verification code rendered as a QR code on the printed document; an invoice failing DGI schema validation is legally ineffective and cannot support ITBMS input credits. The exporter must reconcile the zero-rated e-invoice to the customs DUCA exit record within the DGI portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 1165 of the Código Fiscal applies the 0% rate to goods physically exported from Panamanian customs territory, including IVD microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay analyzers once the export declaration is verified. Article 1165-B extends 0% treatment to services rendered to non-residents and wholly used or exploited abroad, provided the benefit is realized outside Panama; this covers offshore technical support, remote diagnostics, and embedded software licensing for IVD equipment. Conditions: exporter status in the RUC, registration in the VUCE/DUCA customs system, non-resident recipient evidence, no use of the service within Panama, and issuance of a 0%-rated e-invoice referencing the DUCA or export contract.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DUA/DUCA export declaration (Documento Único de Aduana or Declaración Única Centroamericana) endorsed with exit verification by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing physical removal of the goods from Panama to the foreign buyer
Purchase order or sales contract, together with SWIFT LC or TT wire instructions where payment is not prepaid
Inward remittance certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) issued by the receiving Panamanian bank demonstrating crediting of the export proceeds
Certificate of origin and MINSA/DNFD sanitary registration certificate for medical devices when required by customs or the DGI
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI cross-references the DUCA exit record against banking evidence of inward remittances; if the foreign-currency proceeds are not credited to a Panama bank account within 180 days, the transaction is recharacterized as a domestic taxable supply and the ITBMS is clawed back at 7% plus monthly compound interest (1.5% per month) and statutory surcharges. Administrative sanctions under articles 700-722 of the Código Fiscal range from 25% to 200% of the tax omitted; false declarations, fictitious bills of lading, or circular remittance arrangements expose the entity to criminal defraudación fiscal prosecution with imprisonment, suspension of the exporter RUC registration, and joint liability against the resident agent in abuse-of-form cases. The assessment statute of limitations is three years for filed taxpayers and six years for non-filers, during which retrospective clawback and penalties may be imposed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama is a fully dollarized economy with no national central bank or lender of last resort. The monetary policy anchor is the U.S. dollar, and monetary decisions are functionally delegated to the U.S. Federal Reserve System. The banking regulator and licensing authority is the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, SBP) under Decree-Law No. 9 of 1998. Financial intelligence and anti-money-laundering supervision rest with the Financial Analysis Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero, UAF). Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent and settlement bank for the State payment system, while the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) sets the framework for public-sector financial and risk management.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: There are no exchange controls. Under the Decree-Law No. 9 of 1970 monetary regime, both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible into U.S. dollars at a legal 1:1 Balboa/USD par; the Balboa exists only as a nominal unit with fractional coins. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, repayment of intra-group loans, and liquidation proceeds may be transferred abroad freely without SBP or MEF licenses. The practical hurdle is documentary rather than regulatory: the paying bank must classify the transaction under its SWIFT MT103 repatriation codes, provide a valid underlying agreement and beneficiary tax certificate, and comply with UAF suspicious-transaction reporting thresholds. Panamanian-source profit is subject separately to territorial income tax and a 10% dividend tax at distribution, but this is a fiscal liability, not a currency-convertibility barrier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panamanian law imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation of export proceeds. An IVD manufacturer may retain 100% of documentary-export receipts in USD or foreign-currency accounts, including offshore nostro accounts, and may freely allocate such funds to capital expenditure, operational disbursements, or dividends. The only obligations arise from AML/CFT due diligence: for each settlement exceeding USD 10,000, or where an aggregate suspicion pattern exists, the receiving bank must hold on file the commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, packing list, purchase order, and end-user certification for medical devices, all consistent with the UAF regulatory framework.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium as a primary treasury route. Panama does not license offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, or Payoneer as banks; such providers cannot join the local ACH-Panama clearing system, cannot open SBP-regulated nostro accounts, and lack the SBP licensing status required to accept client deposits in Panama. Foreign EMIs may be used solely for micro-disbursements under USD 20,000 per ticket and for supplementary payment cards. A Panama-authorized payment-service provider regulated under Law 23 of 2015, offering virtual-account capability, is viable as a secondary collection rail only after full mirror-KYC, while the primary cash-management relationship must sit with a licensed commercial bank to preserve UAF reporting and documentary-export evidence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A general physical appearance is not required by SBP banking regulations, but individual bank licensing policy almost always demands a documented identity interview for ultimate beneficial owners and account signatories. For non-resident S.A. shareholders, the standard path is a notarized, apostilled identity packet plus a video-conference interview accepted under the bank's risk-based due-diligence manual, with occasional in-person contact at a Panama City, Miami, or regional representative office. Fully remote onboarding is only feasible for pre-vetted introducers, such as licensed Panamanian law-firm clients, and for low-risk natural persons holding long-term Panama residence; a 100% digital, no-human-interaction opening for an operating medical-device manufacturer is not generally available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Historic or suspected bearer-share structure, unnamed UBOs, or a registered-agent continuity gap in an offshore S.A.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the original apostilled corporate charter (Testimonio), current padron (shareholder registry), notarized resolution appointing the account signatory, registered-agent letter of continuity, RUC certificate, UBO declaration under Law 254 of 2021, and sourcing statement tracing initial capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flag from invoice mismatches, overpriced medical-device components, or irregular prepayment percentages in the supplier network.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a trade pack per shipment: proforma and final commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, packing list, certificate of origin, MINSA-DGIS health-registry approval for the IVD analyzer, ISO 13485 certificate, transfer-pricing analysis if intra-group, supplier KYC documentation, and end-user declarations for the microfluidic cartridges.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance concern: management and manufacturing cash flows appear to pass through a shell with no local payroll, office lease, or operational evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide Panama office lease, payroll records for operational staff, municipal operating license (Aviso de Operación), DGI RUC registration, filed income-tax returns and monthly form 940/941 declarations, plant photographs, utility invoices, and a supplemental narrative of the local assembly and quality-control process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-speed in-and-out flows, transfers to or from sanctioned or grey-listed jurisdictions, or unexplained third-party payments soon after account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a one-year cash-flow forecast, source-of-funds affidavit, corporate ownership chart, commercial agreements with customers and vendors, end-user declarations, and a transaction-rationale memorandum; commit to transacting only through U.S.-cleared correspondent channels.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inject equity or shareholder loans exclusively in USD through Fedwire or CHIPS into the S.A.'s USD account using the exact corporate legal name and RUC. In SWIFT remittance information include the purpose code and reference: Capital Contribution - Share Subscription, or Shareholder Loan - Intercompany. No exchange-control license or central-bank authorization is needed in Panama. Remitters in capital-control jurisdictions must first complete their own overseas-investment authorization; Panama neither conditions nor validates that step. The receiving bank will conduct standard source-of-funds verification: board resolution approving the injection, updated public-registry excerpt, apostilled powers of attorney, and a notarized capital-report statement. For intra-group funding tranches above USD 50,000, provide the group consolidated budget or lender board minutes. Although the minimum paid-in capital under Panamanian law is zero, subscribe at least USD 1,000 in common shares and reflect the paid-in entry in the padron to assist the registered-agent attestation and account-opening reviewers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 direct wires for prepayments and partial milestones, keeping any single prepayment under 20% of the purchase order. For supplier tickets above USD 50,000, issue irrevocable UCP 600 documentary letters of credit via SWIFT MT700, with documents complying with UCP 600 and ISBP 745. For small consignment lanes, documentary collection (DP/DA) under URC 522 is acceptable. Draw trade loans using evidenced purchase orders to finance inventory; prefer at-sight LC drafts over 90-day deferred LC to minimise withholding implications on interest and to keep the document flow tight. Every disbursement must cross-reference the commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, and the manufacturer's MINSA medical-device import/export registration, preserving a complete UAF audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC deliverable foreign-exchange forwards on USD vs. EUR, GBP, CHF, JPY, or CAD, executed with SBP-licensed banks or offshore dealers under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a CSA credit-support annex.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on regional Latin-American currencies such as COP, BRL, MXN, or CLP as a hedge of sourcing or re-export exposure without mobilizing underlying notional.

Cross-currency swaps, including coupon-only and principal-exchange structures, and cross-currency interest-rate swaps under an ISDA master with an investment-grade dealer, permissible since Panama is not a restrictive FX jurisdiction.
FX swaps and forward rolls, including spot-to-forward and forward-forward ladder trades, via the treasury desk of the primary relationship bank.
Vanilla OTC currency options, both calls and puts on non-USD currencies, permitted under local law and priced offshore, subject to the bank's derivatives-eligibility assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax — Tasa Única de Mantenimiento (standard S.A. with authorized capital of US$10,000 or less)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year obligation payable annually no later than 31 March; first-year payment may be prorated for newly incorporated entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues statutory surcharge and monthly default interest; persistent non-payment blocks official certificates and may trigger administrative strike-off proceedings before the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return — Declaración de Renta Anual
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before 31 March following the close of the calendar tax year; non-calendar fiscal years must file within three months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and non-filing are subject to fines under the Panamanian Tax Code, monthly default interest on tax due, suspension of the taxpayer ID for official transactions, and risk of administrative dissolution after repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Report — Informe Anual de la Sociedad
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección Mercantil
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing window is 1 January through 30 June of each calendar year; the licensed resident agent files on behalf of the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Filings made after 30 June incur a registry late surcharge; failure to file for consecutive years marks the company as inactive and can ultimately result in administrative strike-off from the Public Registry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Law 52 of 2016, a mandatory independent audit and filing of audited financial statements are required for legal entities with annual gross income exceeding US$3,000,000 or total assets exceeding US$3,000,000, and for entities designated as large taxpayers (gran contribuyente) by the DGI; lower-turnover manufacturing S.A.s must keep proper accounting records and file financial statements but may submit accountant-compiled statements where no statutory audit threshold is met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB and adopted by the Colegio de Contadores Públicos de Panamá; eligible smaller entities may apply IFRS for SMEs; financial statements are presented in United States dollars and reported in Balboas per Panamanian practice.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Law 23 of 2015, as amended, requires the licensed resident agent to obtain and maintain a current record of ultimate beneficial owners. The company must provide an annual sworn confirmation confirming no change in beneficial ownership, or an updated confirmation within 30 calendar days of any share transfer or economic-ownership change; reportable UBO changes are also filed in the DGI's Registro de Transparencia y Beneficiarios Finales within the statutory updating deadline.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$300–US$800 per year for licensed resident agent and registered office for a standard Panama S.A., excluding government taxes and filing fees
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,000–US$8,000 for a dormant or low-volume S.A.; US$10,000–US$25,000 for an active IVD manufacturing entity required to present audited statutory financial statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on Panama-source income only; foreign-source income excluded under territorial taxation
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for manufacturing; reduced 5% withholding on dividends paid from profits taxed at the entity level; 100% deduction of costs and expenses attributable to Panama-source revenue; no tax on foreign branch income; possible partial exemptions under Ley 41 de 2007 for certain strategic service exports if qualifying application approved

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2000 (Informe de Renta / Declaración de Renta) filed electronically through DGI's portal 'E-Tax 2.0' (Sistema de Declaración de Renta en Línea); annual income tax return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline extended per terminal digit of the corporate RUC ('Registro Único de Contribuyente') over the months of March, April, May, June, July and August following the fiscal year-end (31 December); final payment due with the return; fiscal year may be a different 12-month period only with prior DGI approval

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC number, corporate name, fiscal year-end date, and registered address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the local tax identification number issued by DGI for the Panama S.A. and the local registered agent's address; non-resident shareholders are not listed individually

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income deemed derived from Panama, including sales of IVD microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay analyzers delivered or used in Panama, service fees, and any other Panama-source receipts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue with Panamanian situs; export sales to foreign customers are excluded from taxable gross income and should be supported by bills of lading and foreign purchase orders

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 103 - Cost of Sales and Direct Costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of raw materials, components, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead attributable to taxable Panama-source revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the manufacturing plant is in Panama and goods are exported, allocate costs to exported revenue; only costs attributable to local sales reduce taxable income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Line 104 - Operating and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible selling, general, administrative, depreciation, amortization, and other operating expenses related to Panama-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses incurred abroad for foreign sales are not deductible against Panama-source income unless properly allocated and supported by invoices, contracts, and wire records; transfer-pricing adjustments apply for cross-border related-party purchases

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 105 - Non-Deductible Provisions and Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible items: income tax paid, fines, gifts, excess reserves, and expenses without receipts or proper withholding
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any payment to non-resident related parties without adequate documentation or subject to WHT at reduced rates without TRC is non-deductible

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Line 106 - Net Taxable Income (Base Imponible)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed as gross Panama-source income less allowable deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure no foreign-source income is erroneously included; maintain an internal foreign/domestic income allocation schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable rate (25%) applied to net taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the standard 25% rate; no progressive rate applies to corporations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Line 108 - Tax Credits and Withholdings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments, withholding credits, and any creditable tax paid in Panama
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Panamanian tax withheld on local sales and services; foreign tax credits are not available under territorial taxation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 / Line 109 - Balance Due or Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax remitted with the return or carried as credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Wire payment in USD (Panama's legal currency) through the DGI electronic payment system; no payment is due on excluded foreign income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Informational disclosure of foreign income excluded from tax, including foreign export sales, foreign IP royalties, and foreign branch profits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete this annex for the IVD exporting entity; attach schedules of export invoices, foreign bank statements, and intercompany agreements establishing the foreign situs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of 5% of the tax due for the first month and 1.5% per additional month or fraction thereof, up to a maximum of 10%; late payment surcharge of 1.5% per month or fraction thereof, up to 25%; fines for non-filing of Form 2000 range from USD 100 to USD 500 plus 10% of unpaid tax; administrative interest up to 10% annual; criminal sanctions for fraudulent non-filing

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid out of profits not yet subject to income tax; 5% on dividends paid out of profits already taxed at the corporate level (post-2019 reform, effective for fiscal year 2020 onwards); the 5% dividend WHT is credited or treated as final payment
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's double tax treaty network is extremely limited; there are no comprehensive DTAs with major trading partners such as the United States, China, the EU Member States, or Latin American manufacturing peers; where a limited treaty exists (e.g., Mexico by Aviso 233-2015 and certain agreement with Argentina not yet ratified), the non-resident must provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty-state tax authority, accompanied by a sworn statement and Form 2009 (Aplicación de Beneficio de Convenio para Evitar la Doble Tributación) submitted to the DGI before payment; DGI reviews and approves reduced WHT rates on a case-by-case basis; in practice, most dividend and royalty outflows are taxed at the full statutory domestic WHT rates
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalty/technical assistance payments to non-residents is 12.5% on gross amounts paid for the use of trademarks, patents, copyrights, know-how, and similar intangibles; interest paid to non-residents by local companies is subject to 12.5% unless paid to a licensed international bank or on loans registered in Panama (exempt); treaty rates are negligible due to the absence of comprehensive DTAs; there is no WHT on management fees paid from Panama-source funds, but the expense is deductible only if the services are necessary and actually rendered

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama's transfer pricing rules (Ley 52 de 2015, amended by Ley 120 de 2019) apply to transactions between a Panama taxpayer and its non-resident related parties; documentation (Local File and Master File) is mandatory only when the taxpayer's aggregate related-party transaction volume exceeds USD 1,000,000 in the fiscal year; no separate Panamanian country-by-country reporting threshold; CbCR obligations apply to ultimate parent groups with consolidated revenue above USD 750,000,000 under OECD-aligned rules
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not have a UK-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime; however, the Corporate Income Tax law adopts territorial-source taxation and the 'substance-over-form' doctrine to deny the situs of income if only formalities are performed in Panama; the Dirección General de Ingresos can re-characterize transactions where central management, decision-making, or core revenue-generating activities for export sales are located outside Panama; additionally, Panama's updated 'Sistema de Intercambio de Información' and OECD Inclusive Framework membership require beneficial ownership information, economic substance information, and transfer pricing documentation for related-party dealings; a Panama S.A. holding only IP without personnel, premises, or operational capacity remains exposed to BEPS Action Plan 5 and 13 reviews

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a knowingly false Form 2000, omitting Panama-source income, overstating deductions, or concealing the existence of a Panama operating plant and local sales
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under Articles 114 and 115 of Código Penal (Delitos contra el Fisco); imprisonment from 2 to 4 years; fines of USD 50,000 to USD 100,000; disgorgement of unpaid tax plus interest at 10% annual and late payment surcharges up to 25%
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, resident agents, and beneficial owners who sign or knowingly direct a fraudulent return face criminal prosecution, travel bans, extradition exposure under the Inter-American Convention on Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters, and personal civil liability for the corporation's unpaid tax if corporate assets are insufficient

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Panama Sociedad Anónima that files nil tax returns, claims zero taxable income, or holds foreign IVD intangibles and generates substantial exports but has no physical manufacturing site, no employees, no bank account in Panama, or no independent decision-making
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterization of foreign-source income as Panama-source taxable income under substance-over-form; assessment of 25% corporate income tax on the full amount re-characterized; obligation to register transfer pricing documentation; fines from USD 5,000 to USD 40,000 for failure to maintain accounting records; cancellation of the 'agente residente' license
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held jointly liable for unpaid tax under Law 52 of 2016 if they vote to distribute dividends without making the WHT or knowingly approve transactions lacking economic substance; travel restrictions may issue upon a tax lien exceeding USD 10,000

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to disclose the ultimate beneficial owner in the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (activated by Law 23 of 2015, implemented 2019-2021), accepting bearer shares without converting to registered shares, or allowing wire transfers for IVD device payments without local AML compliance files
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines from USD 500 to USD 1,000,000 per violation of Law 23 de 2015 (AML/CFT regime); criminal money laundering penalties up to 5 to 10 years imprisonment under Código Penal Article 254-B; freezing of corporate bank accounts; administrative dissolution for failure to appoint resident agent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face joint personal liability, seizure of personal assets, imprisonment, and inclusion in international AML blacklists; panama gaming and financing licensing authorities may revoke operating permits for the IVD manufacturing entity

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border dividend distribution to the non-resident parent without applying the required 5% or 10% dividend WHT, or payment of royalties for microfluidic technology at artificially reduced rates to shift profits abroad without a valid DTA and transfer pricing study
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding tax deficiency assessed on the gross dividend or royalty payment at the applicable rate (5%, 10%, or 12.5%) plus interest from the time payment was due; penalty for failure to withhold equals 100% of the unremitted WHT; non-deductibility of the royalty expense; transfer pricing adjustment to taxable income plus penalty of 10% of the adjustment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve a dividend distribution before the withholding obligation is satisfied are jointly and severally personally liable for the withholding tax; travel bans and restriction of professional licenses apply to 'repeat offenders'; imprisonment of 1 to 3 years for aggravated withholding tax fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intercompany purchase of microfluidic cartridges, analyzers, or raw material components from a related party exceeding USD 1,000,000 in aggregate without preparing a Local File, Master File, or transfer pricing study with contemporaneous substantiation of CUP/TNMM testing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of between 1% and 5% of the assessed transfer pricing adjustment if documentation is missing or defective; mandatory filing of a sworn statement and full TP annex to Form 2000; interest and surcharges on the primary tax adjustment; refusal of export price deductions; publication in the DGI's defaulting taxpayers list
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and tax officers bear personal liability for negligence in preparing or approving TP documentation; if the TP default accompanies a deliberate evasion scheme, principal actors face criminal sanctions as tax offenders

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register the commercial banking relationship or file annual automatic exchange forms to disclose accounts held for the U.S.-based parent or U.S. beneficial owners of the Panama S.A. and failure to safeguard wire-transfer know-your-customer records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under Law 23 of 2015 for non-compliance with beneficial ownership register; coordinated penalties from the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) for bank account-linked AML deficiencies up to USD 100,000; possible closure of the corporate bank account and mandatory audits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability attaches for AML compliance officers and directors who knowingly sign false beneficial ownership declarations; U.S. DOJ and IRS extraterritorial charges could target the parent as a 'qualified intermediary' failure, with civil penalties up to 50% of the USD value transacted
